name: Whisker Sensory Array
description: Induces growth of functional vibrissae (whiskers) on the cheeks, modeled on cat sensory whiskers. The whiskers are 8–12 cm long, stiffer than hair, and rooted in deep follicles surrounded by mechanoreceptor nerve endings. They detect air currents, vibrations, proximity to surfaces, and spatial dimensions with extraordinary sensitivity. A whisker user can navigate in total darkness by air displacement alone, detect a person approaching from behind by air current disruption, and judge whether they can fit through a gap without measuring. The whiskers are expressive — they fan forward when the user is attentive, flatten when startled, and droop when tired. Combined with cat ears, the result is a facial expression system that broadcasts emotional state through ear position, whisker angle, and eye glow simultaneously.
source_organism: Felis catus (domestic cat), Rattus norvegicus (brown rat, enhanced mechanoreceptor density)
procedure: Facial follicle induction with mechanoreceptor neural integration, 2 sessions
expression_time: 4–6 weeks for whisker growth; neural sensitivity develops over 2 months
reversibility: Removable by follicle ablation; neural sensitivity fades over 6 months
side_effects: Whiskers are sensitive to touch — casual face-touching becomes uncomfortable
Whisker breakage is painful and takes weeks to regrow
Involuntary whisker expression broadcasts emotional state
Wind causes constant low-level sensory input — windy days are 'loud'
social_perception: Adorable to most people. Cat whiskers combined with cat ears create a feline facial aesthetic that is enormously popular in Meridian 88. The expressive whisker movement is considered charming. Some users find the emotional broadcasting embarrassing.
story_hooks: A whisker user detects a vibration pattern in a building's structure that indicates imminent collapse — their sensory array picks up what instruments miss
A community of cat-eared, whiskered residents develops a nonverbal communication system based on ear and whisker positions — a language invisible to unmodified humans
